title: QUIC RFC 9000 MAX_STREAM_DATA Frame Focused Proof
purpose: Describe the bounded RFC 9000 Section 19.10 MAX_STREAM_DATA parser, formatter, stream-credit, and remembered-limit proof slice.
design_summary: The MAX_STREAM_DATA frame remains centered on the existing frame codec, immutable frame view, and connection stream-state bookkeeping. The parser accepts only the fixed one-byte frame type 0x11, then parses Stream ID and Maximum Stream Data as QUIC variable-length integers in that order. Runtime stream state applies the field as an absolute send limit for the affected send-capable stream, rejects locally initiated streams that have not been created, rejects receive-only streams with STREAM_STATE_ERROR, blocks outbound bytes above the largest advertised stream credit, and rejects inbound stream bytes above remembered receive limits with FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
data_and_state_considerations: This slice covers RFC 9000 Section 19.10 frame shape and the stream-credit semantics directly observable through QuicConnectionStreamState. Sparse receive ranges are allowed when reordering makes the largest received offset exceed unique bytes received, but final-size and flow-control checks continue to use the largest known offset and remembered stream limit.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Non-0x11 and non-minimal 0x11 frame-type encodings are rejected by the fixed-type parser.
Truncated Stream ID and Maximum Stream Data variable-length integers are rejected before a frame view is produced.
The parser consumes exactly the MAX_STREAM_DATA frame and leaves following frames for the packet parser.
MAX_STREAM_DATA updates only the affected stream ID and ignores stale values that do not increase the current send limit.
Receive-only unidirectional streams remain invalid MAX_STREAM_DATA targets even after being opened by inbound STREAM data.
Remembered early-data stream limits are represented by the same receive-limit bookkeeping used for 0-RTT and normal STREAM frame admission.
alternatives_considered: Leave S19P10 under broad frame-codec and flow-control tests; rejected because generated triage still showed missing focused proof and broad-proof warnings.
Change the frame parser to validate stream directionality; rejected because stream-state validity depends on endpoint role and current stream registry state, not the frame-codec wire shape.
Broaden this slice into full 0-RTT receive admission; rejected because managed server 0-RTT receive remains explicitly closed outside the remembered-limit bookkeeping floor.
risks: This proof does not claim public 0-RTT receive support or server anti-replay admission.
Parser rejection proves malformed frame handling at the codec seam, not a hosted endpoint close-packet assertion for every malformed input.
The slice proves current stream-state bookkeeping semantics and does not add new public flow-control APIs.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers RFC 9000 Section 19.10 MAX_STREAM_DATA parser, formatter, affected-stream credit handling, send-limit enforcement, sparse receive accounting, and remembered stream-limit violations for requirements 0001 through 0014 only.
